blocks.heading: Benefits and costs of participation
blocks.text: Participation can improve decisions through worker knowledge, increase acceptance of change, build trust and provide responsibility and recognition. It can also take time, create disputes about representation, expose confidential information or disappoint staff if limits are unclear. The outcome depends on genuine influence, relevant competence and management response. Consulting without listening can damage rather than strengthen trust. The number of people involved should fit the scope and urgency of the issue. A benefit and a disadvantage are not competing definitions; weigh them against the actual circumstances.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Luma Repairs invites technicians to improve job scheduling but never replies to their proposals. The invitation offers potential useful information, yet the missing response can make staff regard the process as token participation. Set clear boundaries, assess proposals and explain decisions.
